candidates.summary: altitude: BuildPlan calls LoadPkgs itself, so testing the derivation needs a 38-line on-disk monorepo and ten full tree walks; the fix is a pure `plan(pkgs, changed, max)` under it
candidates.failure_scenario: Every question the table asks (is this realm a dependent, does the cap keep the changed one, do seed realms get appended) is about a package graph, not about the filesystem, but BuildPlan's first statement is `LoadPkgs(root)`, so each case has to be expressed as files under t.TempDir() and each subtest re-walks and re-parses the whole fixture tree. The cost shows in what the table cannot say: a case needing a draft package, a cycle, an unparseable .gno or a realm above the cap is a new set of files rather than a new literal, which is why maxRealms is exercised with one realm and a cap of one. Splitting the graph derivation into a function over `map[string]*Pkg` leaves BuildPlan as loader plus call, lets the table hold Pkg literals, and keeps the one fakeRepo case for LoadPkgs itself.
candidates.verify_by: extract the body of BuildPlan after LoadPkgs into `func planFrom(pkgs map[string]*Pkg, changed []string, maxRealms int) *Plan`, have BuildPlan call it, and run cd misc/gnopreview && go test ./...
